the prevalence and correlates of caregiver psychiatric morbidity.

dementia caregiving in Egypt is a high-risk factor for psychiatric morbidity, and this morbidity was related to the sociodemographic and the clinical variables of the caregiver, the patient, and the patient’s disease.
caregivers of dementia patients are more vulnerable than other groups of caregivers and that the more burden they have, the more vulnerable they become.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
caregivers of patients with chronic diseases are at a higher risk for psychiatric morbidity and caregiver’s burden.
the burden of caregiving is not only a physical burden but also a psychological burden.
caregivers of patients with AD and other dementias are at high risk for psychiatric morbidity.

caregiver’s burden and psychiatric morbidity are highly correlated with the patient’s cognitive impairment, activities of daily living, and behavioral and psychiatric symptoms of dementia.
